title: Create meal-plan shopping list generation service
description: Add `CreateShoppingListFromMealPlanService` to load meal plans, resolve referenced recipes, tolerate per-recipe read/parse failures, compute scaling factors, and aggregate scaled recipes with existing aisle infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: `CookbookApp/MealPlans/CreateShoppingListFromMealPlanService.swift` defines the requested service and `CreateError` cases.
The service reads the meal plan through existing helpers, resolves recipe references, parses recipes, and skips failed recipe loads with logging.
Scaling factor uses plan-reference servings divided by recipe metadata servings, defaulting to `1.0` when either side is unavailable or non-serving based.
The service calls `AggregatedShoppingList.aggregate(recipes:aisleConfig:)` with scaled recipes and existing aisle configuration.

handoff_summary.completed:
- `CreateShoppingListFromMealPlanService` implemented with `CreateError` (readPlanFailed, writeFailed, listAlreadyExists) and `create(planURL:named:recipesFolder:aisleConfig:) throws -> URL` static method.
- Duplicate-name check before any I/O.
- Reads plan via `MealPlanFiles.readText` + `MealPlanParser.parse`.
- Resolves each `MealPlanRecipe.path` to a `.cook` URL under `recipesFolder`, parsing via `CooklangParser.canonical.parse`; per-recipe read/parse failures are skipped with a `print` log.
- Scale factor = plan-reference-servings / recipe-metadata-servings, defaulting to 1.0 when reference has no numeric servings-unit quantity, or when recipe metadata lacks a positive servings value.
- Calls `AggregatedShoppingList.aggregate(recipes:aisleConfig:)` with all scaled recipes.
- Builds provenance bullets as `**<block heading>** — <display name>` via `addMealsEntry` per occurrence.
- Writes rendered markdown via `ShoppingListFiles.writeText`.
- `xcodebuild` build succeeds; `xcodegen generate` was run prior to the build to include the new file.
handoff_summary.remaining: View-layer wiring in `MealPlanDetailView.swift`: replace the `showShoppingListStub` stub alert with the create-list alert, confirmation alert, and "View" sheet presenting `ShoppingListDetailView`. This is the UI integration bead that should follow.
handoff_summary.risks: The service claims security-scoped access on `recipesFolder` for recipe reads, but individual recipe URLs are constructed by appending a path under `recipesFolder`. If the plan references recipes outside `recipesFolder` (e.g., absolute paths), those reads will silently skip — consistent with the error-tolerance design but worth noting.
handoff_summary.next_action: Wire `CreateShoppingListFromMealPlanService.create` into `MealPlanDetailView`: replace the stubbed `showShoppingListStub` alert with a create-name alert, call the service on confirm, show a confirmation alert with "View" / "OK", and present `ShoppingListDetailView` in a sheet on "View".
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None — new file only, no modifications to shared files.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Scale factor defaults to 1.0 (not 0.0) when the recipe's servings metadata is zero or absent, preventing ingredient quantities from being zeroed out. The `recipeServings > 0` guard achieves this.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: No tests written — test execution is the tester agent's responsibility. Service is fully unit-testable via a temp-folder fixture pattern identical to `AddToShoppingListService` tests.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: Inner sub-section names (`Lunch` / `Dinner`) are intentionally excluded from provenance bullets per spec v1 scope. Inline `MealPlanItem.ingredient` entries are silently skipped.

conflict_risks: None — new file only, no modifications to shared files.

execution_history.summary: Created `CookbookApp/MealPlans/CreateShoppingListFromMealPlanService.swift` with enum-based static service that loads a meal plan, resolves and parses referenced recipes (tolerating failures with logging), computes scaling factors from plan-reference vs. recipe-metadata servings, aggregates scaled recipes via `AggregatedShoppingList.aggregate`, builds a `ShoppingListDocument` with per-recipe provenance bullets, and writes the result. Build succeeds cleanly.
